title: The Dual-Functional Monoterpenes D-Carvone and Carveol in Citrus-Drop Essential Oil Reprogram Listeria monocytogenes Biofilms via an Escape-Induction and Metabolic-Lethality Synergistic Strategy
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes (LM) poses a significant threat to food safety due to its ability to form persistent biofilms. Thus, developing efficient and green strategies to combat biofilms is crucial in combating LM. This study evaluates the antibiofilm activity and mechanisms of essential oils (EOs) extracted from citrus physiological fruit drop (CPFD), an agricultural byproduct, against LM. Among eight CPFD-EOs, Ougan ( Citrus reticulata cv. Suavissima) fruit drop essential oil (OGEO) exhibited the highest extraction yield (3.18%) and was found to have a unique chemical profile characterized by enrichment in oxygenated monoterpenes, particularly D -carvone and carveol. OGEO demonstrated the strongest broad-spectrum antibacterial and antibiofilm activity, with two of its components, D -carvone and carveol, showing significant synergistic antibacterial effects (the fractional inhibitory concentration (FIC) index = 0.5). More specifically, OGEO and its monoterpenes damaged bacterial cell membranes and disrupted biofilm architecture. Integrated transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed a multi-target mechanism: OGEO simultaneously inhibits carbon metabolism, nucleotide synthesis, adenosine triphosphate-binding cassette (ABC) transporters, and cell wall biosynthesis, while enhancing bacterial chemotaxis and flagellar assembly, inducing biofilm-embedded cells to “escape” from the protective matrix into a vulnerable planktonic state. D- Carvone possibly acts by disrupting cell wall integrity and inducing this “escape” (structural stripping + escape induction), while carveol mainly causes the collapse of glycolysis and amino acid metabolism (metabolic lethality). The synergy of these compounds constitutes a novel escape induction + lethal clearance synergistic model against biofilms. Our study demonstrates that CPFD-derived EOs, particularly OGEO, are a promising source of natural antibiofilm agents. Their multi-target synergistic action effectively combats LM biofilms, providing a theoretical basis for the valorization of agricultural waste and the development of novel food antimicrobial strategies.

title: Pseudo-Aggregation: Microplastic Input Induces Apparent but Unstable Soil Structure in Agricultural Soils
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) are increasingly recognized as emerging soil pollutants that alter soil structure and function, yet the mechanisms through which they reshape soil aggregation remain poorly understood. Here, we coupled a nationwide paired field survey with uniform-sized aggregate reconstructions, i.e., large macroaggregates (LMA, > 5 mm); medium-sized aggregates (MEA, 0.25–5 mm); and microaggregates (MIA, < 0.25 mm), to investigate how MPs influence soil aggregate turnover across the disintegration–formation–stabilization stages. We validated the pseudo-aggregation hypothesis that MPs physically reinforce mechanical aggregate stability but fail to sustain water-stable structures. Field observations showed that plastic inputs significantly increased the mean weight diameter (MWD) and geometric mean diameter (GMD) under dry sieving (MWD_D and GMD_D, respectively) but did not improve water stability indices (the above two parameters under wet sieving, i.e., MWD_W and GMD_W), and also increased the percentage of aggregate destruction (PAD). Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and random forest analyses further indicated that MPs strongly promoted mechanical stability, whereas water stability and PAD were primarily associated with soil properties, soil nutrients, and microbial activity. In 210-day laboratory reconstructions, MPs generally slowed the disintegration of LMA and promoted the formation of MIA, confirming their structural but not functional reinforcement. Collectively, these results identify LMA as the main fraction affected by MP-induced pseudo-aggregation and highlight water stability as a key metric for soil-structure risk assessment and agricultural management.

title: Fluid MIMO: A Timely MIMO Upgrade
AI Systems and the Future of Research: Ten Observations on a New Human–AI Partnership
Artificial-Intelligence-Guided Weed Management with Herbicides, Lasers, and Robotic Cultivators: Opportunities, Limitations, and Unintended Consequences
Extended Reality as a New Farming Tool for Enhancing Smart Agriculture and Precision Farming
abstract: Extended reality (XR) is increasingly being explored as a new farming tool that links digital information with physical agricultural environments. Although studies have reported the potential of XR-based human–computer interfaces for agricultural decision-making, operations, and training, the technological pathways, effectiveness, and interdisciplinary implications of these approaches remain incompletely synthesized. This scoping review examines XR application models, enabling technologies, and implementation across crop monitoring, livestock and aquaculture management, agricultural machinery, and education. The reviewed studies indicate that XR can support task-specific perception–analysis–visualization–guidance workflows and may facilitate a shift from experience-based to data-informed decisions, with improvements in precision, efficiency, and safety reported under the tested conditions. We further map the XR technology spectrum and its integration with key enabling technologies, highlighting how these factors jointly shape system performance and field-deployment potential. Major barriers include outdoor adaptability, deployment cost, software integration, data privacy, and limited long-term validation in real agricultural environments. Further progress requires technological integration, interdisciplinary collaboration, cost control, and user-centered design. This review provides researchers, developers, and practitioners with a roadmap for XR solutions that address practical agricultural needs and support greener, more intelligent, and sustainable production.

title: Agentic AI-Native Collaborative Task Offloading and Resource Orchestration for 6G Space–Air-Integrated Computing Power Networks
abstract: The advent of the sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication era heralds a paradigm shift from terrestrial-centric connectivity to a three-dimensional, ubiquitous ecosystem known as the space–air-integrated computing power network (SAICPN). This architecture integrates low-Earth-orbit satellites and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) with terrestrial networks to provide seamless computation offloading and edge intelligence services to ground users, particularly in underserved remote regions and emerging low-altitude economies. However, the realization of SAICPN is hindered by severe resource orchestration challenges. These challenges arise from the high-speed orbital dynamics of satellites, the nonlinear aerodynamic energy constraints of UAVs, and the intricate dependency structures of modern computational tasks modeled as directed acyclic graphs. Conventional centralized optimization schemes incur prohibitive signaling overhead, while traditional multi-agent reinforcement learning frameworks struggle with the instability and partial observability inherent in such large-scale, heterogeneous networks. This paper proposes a novel agentic artificial intelligence framework: the generative agentic interface-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (GAI-MADDPG) algorithm. We mathematically model the computation offloading and resource pricing problem as a hierarchical Stackelberg game, providing a rigorous proof of the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium using backward induction and Hessian matrix analysis. Uniquely, our framework integrates variational autoencoders to compress high-dimensional, continuous environmental states into robust latent representations, enabling proactive, intent-based agentic decision-making. Extensive simulations demonstrate that GAI-MADDPG significantly outperforms comparison approaches, achieving a 15%–20% reduction in energy consumption and a 96.5% task completion rate under dynamic, constraints-intensive 6G scenarios. Ablation studies corroborate that each core module makes an indispensable contribution to overall performance.

title: Vision–Language–Action Models for Agricultural Robotics: A Review Towards Embodied Intelligence
abstract: The shift toward Agriculture 5.0 demands robotic systems that can reason and act reliably in unstructured, high-entropy environments. Conventional agricultural robots, limited by rigid modular pipelines, often fail to generalize across diverse crop morphologies and rapidly changing field conditions. In contrast to existing surveys on general-purpose robotics, this paper provides a comprehensive review of vision–language–action (VLA) collaborative intelligence systems. It proposes a transformative framework that integrates multimodal foundation models to bridge the cognitive gap in agricultural robotics. We systematically examine VLA architectures along three core dimensions tailored to agricultural constraints: ① Perception—moving from closed-set detection to open-vocabulary recognition and three-dimensional (3D) visual affordance, leveraging models such as contrastive language–image pre-training (CLIP) and segment anything model (SAM) to mitigate severe foliage occlusion; ② Cognition—employing large language models (LLMs) with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to enable domain-specific reasoning and task decomposition; and ③ Action—advancing toward end-to-end visuomotor policies, with a focus on diffusion policies and sim-to-real transfer frameworks designed for delicate soft-body manipulation. We further discuss key deployment challenges, including efficient edge computing and safety alignment. The review concludes by outlining future directions toward agricultural world models (AWMs) and heterogeneous swarm intelligence, offering a strategic roadmap for next-generation smart farming.

title: Microstructure and Properties of Aluminum/Iron Joints Laser Welded with Nonuniform Heat Input
abstract: In this study, a novel laser welding process scheme for dissimilar steel/aluminum materials, namely, a welding process scheme with nonuniform heat input, is proposed. Al–Si-coated 22MnB5 steel and 6061-T6 aluminum alloy were lap-welded using a welding process scheme with nonuniform heat input, and the result was compared with that of a traditional welding process scheme. As the laser power increased, the mechanical performance of the welded joint initially increased but subsequently decreased. The experimental results indicated that under identical heat input conditions, the novel welding process resulted in high-quality welded joints, and the samples exhibited excellent performance in mechanical tests, with their mechanical properties surpassing those of the joints produced using the traditional uniform heat input welding process by 64% and the average elongation increased by approximately 113%. Owing to the significant differences in the morphology of the weld seams under the two different welding processes, the nail-shaped weld seam altered the fracture path of the welded joint during the tensile test. The fracture mode transitioned from brittle fracture to a combination of crispy and ductile fractures. Finite element modeling simulations were conducted to analyze the reason for the improvement in the mechanical performance of the weld seam. The results revealed that the nail-shaped weld seam shifted the region of stress concentration in mechanical tests.

title: Multifunctional Bone Cements in Regenerative Medicine
From Large-Scale Elastomer Data to Engineering Simulation: A Generalizable Skip-Connected Physics-Informed Neural Network for Hyperelastic Constitutive Modeling
abstract: Hyperelastic constitutive models (HCMs) are essential for accurately describing elastomeric mechanical responses and supporting the structural optimization of engineering rubber products. However, existing empirical parametric and neural-network HCMs often face a trade-off between fitting accuracy and material stability. Here, a skip-connected physics-informed neural network (SC-PINN) was developed as a generalizable, accurate, and stable hyperelastic constitutive modeling framework. The strain energy potential is represented by an invariant-based polyconvex energy neural network, embedding thermodynamic consistency, material objectivity, isotropy, and material stability by construction. A dual skip-connected module is introduced as a physically admissible complementary component. Its output skip pathway can be interpreted as contributing a trainable Mooney–Rivlin-like term corresponding to the first-order terms of the Rivlin polynomial expansion, while the nonlinear backbone provides higher-order-like corrections. The SC-PINN was evaluated on 25 249 experimental uniaxial tensile stress–strain curves and benchmarked against six representative HCMs: Neo-Hookean, Mooney–Rivlin, Ogden, Zhang–Li, unconstrained PINN, and no-skip PINN. This network achieved an average coefficient of determination ( R 2) of 0.9995, with 99.4% of the curves reaching R 2 ≥ 0.99, while maintaining 100% material stability through its polyconvex architecture. Furthermore, the trained SC-PINN was implemented in Abaqus/Standard through a customized UHYPER material subroutine. The implementation was validated across cases ranging from standard specimens to engineering components, including a scaled non-pneumatic tire and the suspension bearings of a heavy-duty truck, with static-stiffness errors below 5.0%. The SC-PINN combines high fitting accuracy, architecture-enforced material stability, and large-scale generalizability. This combination advances hyperelastic constitutive modeling beyond empirical curve fitting toward a physics-grounded, data-driven framework that bridges material characterization and finite-element simulation of engineering elastomeric structures.

title: The Future of Embodied Intelligent Agents in Oilfield Development: Tackling Extreme Wellbore Environments
abstract: As the oil and gas industry advances the exploitation of unconventional reservoirs, onshore ultra-deep formations exceeding 10 000 m in depth and deepwater blocks with water depths greater than 1500 m, downhole operating conditions grow increasingly harsh, with a maximum temperature of 210 °C, peak pressure of 175 MPa, confined borehole spaces and highly corrosive formation fluids. Conventional technologies are increasingly challenged in operating reliably under these extreme downhole conditions. In this context, downhole embodied intelligent agents (DEIAs) constitute a core technical pathway to overcome the aforementioned engineering bottlenecks. This work defines DEIA as an integrated downhole system governed by a closed-loop perception–decision–actuation mechanism, which boasts autonomous decision-making, dynamic environmental adaptability, and multi-agent collaborative operation capabilities. We systematically identify three core challenges arising from practical engineering applications: extreme physical constraints inherent to downhole boreholes, barriers to full-range and high-precision environmental perception, and a severe shortage of robust trainable datasets paired with high-fidelity simulation platforms. Accordingly, we elaborate on three pivotal scientific and technical bottlenecks requiring targeted breakthroughs: the development of intelligent-agent hardware capable of reliable operation under extreme subsurface conditions; reliable kinematic and control algorithms amid coupled multi-physics interference; and sustained long-term operational stability enabled by advanced self-repair material systems. To reconcile the aforementioned technical hurdles with on-site engineering demands, this study establishes a five-dimensional technical development framework customized for major field scenarios, covering layered water injection, complex-condition oil production, hydraulic fracturing, well intervention operations, and durability improvement of DEIAs. This perspective presents a clear development roadmap for the research and field application of DEIAs under extreme energy extraction conditions.

title: Interconnect-Centric AI Computing: From Bandwidth Scaling to Physical Interface Architecture
An International Comparative Analysis of Green Skills Development under Global Climate Governance
Pathways to Sustainable Agriculture in Arid Northwest China: Synergistic Solutions from Water and Land Optimization
abstract: Sustainable agricultural development requires strategies that balance productivity, resource efficiency, and environmental impact to ensure food and water security. In this study, we developed a combined simulation and evaluation framework for major crops (cotton, maize, and wheat) in arid northwest China and proposed a comprehensive agricultural sustainability index (SDG-Ag) to optimize irrigation and crop planting and improve agricultural sustainability. Based on simulations characterized by heterogeneous spatiotemporal variability in crop yield, water requirement, and global warming potential (GWP), our integrated strategy combining irrigation and crop planting structure could achieve a 30.5% irrigation water saving and a 19.4% reduction in GWP while increasing regional crop production by 2.1% until 2090s under two shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs, SSP245, and SSP585), increasing the SDG-Ag score by 30.6%–59.7%. We recommend reducing cultivation in south Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (SXJ) by 3.8%–16.9%, with the reduced area being transferred to north Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region (NXJ) and the Hexi Corridor (HXC). Specifically, this would involve expanding maize by 0.06 million hm 2 in NXJ and expanding cotton by 0.10 million hm 2 in HXC. This integrated strategy could substantially improve agricultural sustainability while prioritizing irrigation optimization (Ir-O) (64.2%–88.7% SDG-Ag enhancement). Our scalable framework paves the way for implementing agricultural sustainability under dynamic climatic and socioeconomic conditions.

title: Micro–Nano Structural Stability of Calcium Silicate Hydrate: A Review
Toward Reliable Asynchronous Brain–Computer Interfaces via Periodic–Aperiodic Feature Integration
abstract: Asynchronous brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) enable users to initiate commands at will, offering a more natural and flexible interaction paradigm compared with conventional synchronous systems. However, accurately distinguishing between intentional control (IC) and non-control (NC) states remains a critical challenge, particularly in noninvasive steady-state visual evoked response (SSVER)-based BCIs. Existing approaches either rely on stimulus-locked periodic features or incorporate auxiliary physiological signals, but their performance is often limited by response variability, nonstationarity, and reduced practicality. In this study, we propose a unified framework that jointly leverages periodic and aperiodic features of neural signals (UFPAF) to enhance state recognition in asynchronous BCIs. Specifically, the proposed method integrates SSVER-based periodic features with aperiodic characteristics derived from the 1/ f -like structure of the power spectrum, enabling a more comprehensive representation of brain activity. We evaluate the proposed framework through extensive offline experiments on both electroencephalography (EEG) and optically pumped magnetometer-based magnetoencephalography (OPM-MEG) data, comparing it with four representative methods, and through online validation in real-time brain-controlled spelling and virtual vehicle control tasks. The results demonstrate that incorporating aperiodic information significantly improves detection accuracy and robustness, particularly under conditions of weak responses and signal variability. These findings underscore the importance of jointly modeling periodic and aperiodic neural dynamics and suggest that the proposed approach provides a promising solution for achieving reliable and naturalistic asynchronous BCI systems.

title: Nanomaterial-Mediated Clearance of Circulating Cell-Free DNA Reduces Periodontitis-Associated Arterial Thrombosis
abstract: Patients with periodontitis exhibit heightened susceptibility to arterial thrombosis, predisposing them to severe cardiovascular events. Gaining insights into the immune mediators linking periodontitis to arterial thrombosis is critical for developing targeted therapeutic strategies. In this study, we demonstrated that elevated plasma levels of cell-free DNA (cfDNA), a key immune mediator, were significantly associated with periodontitis severity, as indicated by increased clinical attachment loss and elevated gingival index scores. Using a combination of human clinical samples and animal models, our research identified a key mechanistic pathway: Periodontitis-induced circulating cfDNA activates Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) signaling, which subsequently triggers platelet activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation to synergistically drive procoagulant responses. In vivo , periodontitis exacerbated arterial thrombus formation and compromised vascular perfusion. Hypothesizing that targeting the cfDNA–TLR9–NET axis would help mitigate periodontitis-promoted thrombosis, biodegradable nanomaterials with a cationic surface were engineered to efficiently clear circulating cfDNA. Administration of these cfDNA scavengers suppressed platelet activation and NETosis both in vitro and in vivo , reduced arterial thrombus burden, and restored vascular perfusion. These functional improvements were accompanied by attenuation of the cfDNA–TLR9–NET cascade and upregulation of vascular contractile gene signatures. These insights highlight the cfDNA–TLR9–NET axis as a potent link between oral and vascular inflammation, offering a promising therapeutic framework to mitigate arterial thrombotic risk in patients with periodontitis.

title: Humanistic Engineering: Why Hybrid Human–AI Cognition Creates a Structural Demand for the Humanities
abstract: Engineering is undergoing a cognitive transformation that the discipline is not yet equipped to name, let alone manage.The deployment of large language models, generative design tools, and autonomous decision-support systems has restructured the cognitive ecology of engineering work itself, altering what engineers need to perceive, judge, articulate, and decide.Engineers now operate within hybrid cognitive systems in which the division of labor between human and machine intelligence is fluid, context-dependent, and constantly renegotiated.Engineering education has begun to register the shift.The most recent revision of the conceive-design-implement-operate (CDIO) Syllabus names digitalization among the drivers of its update and adds knowledge of the social sciences and humanities to its goals [1].The direction is right; the level at which the addition sits limits what it can accomplish.This paper proposes the concept of Humanistic Engineering: the systematic integration of humanistic and artistic competencies into engineering formation and practice as a structural response to the cognitive demands that hybrid humanartificial intelligence (AI) systems place on the human operator.Its theoretical core is what I call second-order prediction, the requirement for the engineer to anticipate the behavior of an AI system by maintaining a generative model of that system's own generative model.I contend that this capacity is structurally analogous to the interpretive challenge the humanities have always trained: modeling another system's interpretive process.The claim is cognitive rather than cultural: Specific cognitive operations are functionally required for performance in hybrid systems, and humanistic practice is the most effective available means of developing them.

title: Evasive Guidance Law Against Proportional Navigation Considering Dynamic Lag
abstract: Terminal-phase evasion serves as a last-resort measure to improve target survivability against missile threats, motivating analytical evasive guidance laws that are both transparent and deployable. However, existing approaches either idealize the target maneuver as a zero-lag input or rely on adjoint integration for online command generation, thereby hindering full exploitation of evasive potential. To address this, an analytical bang-bang evasive guidance law against proportional-navigation (PN)-guided missiles is proposed in this paper, which explicitly incorporates first-order target dynamics and determines the switching direction without online adjoint integration. The key idea is to derive an analytical adjoint representation of this dynamic-lag-aware engagement model and express the associated switching function as a convergent power series, thereby enabling an error-controlled finite-order realization for low-complexity evaluation. Two special cases, corresponding to integer PN gains and matched target-missile time constants, are also derived for further simplification. Representative simulations validate numerical consistency with the adjoint-integration baseline at substantially lower runtime and demonstrate an average miss-distance gain exceeding 2 m over the zero-lag formulation, with broader applicability indicated by Monte Carlo analysis and a three-dimensional (3D) realistic engagement. Hardware deployment on a TMS320F28377D flight controller achieves an approximately 50-fold speedup within typical flight-control timing budgets, supporting practical real-time onboard implementation.

title: Beyond Metamaterials: Metamaterialogy for Broader Material Horizons
Environmental Monitoring as Intelligent Infrastructure: An Engineering Framework for Adaptive Environmental Management
Current Applications and Development Status of Anode Materials with 3D Nanostructures for Sodium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are considered strong alternatives to lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) because of their low cost and the abundance of sodium resources. However, their commercialization is limited by their low capacity, poor cycling stability, and unfavorable redox potentials. Recent advancements have been made in SIBs anode materials, including alloy-based, carbon-based, and three-dimensional (3D) nanostructured materials. Despite these improvements, SIBs anode materials still suffer from an unstable cycle life and slow kinetics. This review focuses on 3D nanostructured anode materials for SIBs. The advantages of various 3D anode materials and their optimization strategies are summarized. In addition, we discuss the potential of developing high-performance SIB anode materials.

title: Advanced Ambient-Energy-Harvesting Technologies for the Autonomous Internet of Things
A Unified Framework for Combinatorial Optimization Based on Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have emerged as powerful tools for solving combinatorial optimization problems (COPs), exhibiting state-of-the-art performance in both graph-structured and non-graph-structured domains. However, existing approaches lack a unified framework capable of addressing a wide range of COPs. After presenting a summary of representative COPs and a brief review of recent advancements in GNNs for solving COPs, this paper proposes a unified framework for solving COPs based on GNNs, including graph representation of COPs, the equivalent conversion of non-graph-structured COPs to graph-structured COPs, graph decomposition, and graph simplification. The proposed framework leverages the ability of GNNs to effectively capture relational information and extract features from graph representations of COPs, offering a generic solution to COPs that can address the limitations of the state of the art in solving non-graph-structured and highly complex graph-structured COPs.

title: Recent Advances in Gel-Free Scalp EEG Electrodes: Materials, Structures, and Fixation Strategies
abstract: In this review, the development of gel-free scalp electroencephalography (EEG) electrodes is summarized from three aspects: material selection, structural design, and head fixation strategies. The focus is on analyzing the role of these factors in balancing the impedance at the electrode–scalp interface with wearing comfort. Electrode materials have evolved from rigid metals to flexible polymers, textiles, and hydrogels, thus mitigating mechanical modulus mismatch with the scalp. Structural design includes optimizing the comb-like configurations of the electrode contact interfaces—such as claw, brush, and arch shapes—coupled with integrated external cushioning structures, such as springs or foams, to increase the contact stability and suppress motion artifacts. Fixation methods have evolved from rigid caps to flexible elastic caps with self-adhesive interfaces, thereby achieving conformable contact, simplified installation, and improved comfort. Collectively, these technological advances provide effective strategies for increasing electrode-scalp coupling stability and signal quality in gel-free EEG systems.

title: Multi-Criteria Evaluation of Lunar Regolith Minerals for In-Situ Thermal Manufacturing and Feedstock Beneficiation
abstract: The heterogeneous mineral composition of lunar regolith significantly influences its thermal forming behavior, posing challenges for in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) in lunar construction. This study characterizes fifteen mineral phases identified from Chang’e-5 and Chang’e -6 returned samples and evaluates the manufacturing suitability of the ten complete-data minerals for three representative thermoforming processes: hot-press sintering (HPS), microwave sintering (MWS), and selective laser melting (SLM). Eight thermophysical properties (solidus temperature, specific heat capacity, thermal conductivity, melt viscosity, surface tension, density, dielectric loss tangent, and solar absorptivity) were characterized for all fifteen minerals. A multi-criteria decision-making framework integrating fuzzy-analytic hierarchy process (AHP)–entropy multiplicative weighting was developed to determine process-specific parameter weights, and the mineral suitability was ranked using dual TOPSIS–VIKOR methods. The combined weights identified thermal conductivity (33.7%) as the dominant parameter for HPS, dielectric loss tangent (57.3%) for MWS, and solar absorptivity (33.0%) for SLM, reflecting the distinct heat transfer mechanisms of each process. For the ten complete-data minerals, a process-specific suitability ranking was established, identifying ilmenite as the only universally superior ranked mineral, the pyroxene group as favorable for HPS and SLM, and the feldspar group as consistently unfavorable across the three processes. Sensitivity analyses (Monte Carlo weight perturbation and VIKOR v -parameter variation) confirmed the robustness of the rankings. Gradient blending experiments validated the predictions at both macroscopic and microscopic scales, with cross-process density correlation yielding Pearson r = 0.788 ( p = 0.002) and Spearman ρ = 0.825 ( p = 0.001), and within-process rank agreement of ρ = 1.000 for all three processes. The findings provide first-order guidance for mineral beneficiation strategies, manufacturing process selection, and preliminary landing-site evaluation in future lunar base construction.

title: Full-Domain Coupler: A Wireless Native Neural Backbone for Channel Representation and Deduction
abstract: Data representation is a fundamental issue in deep learning. However, as wireless data scale and deeply couple across many physical domains such as time, space, and frequency, existing wireless artificial intelligence (AI) technologies lack dedicated representation solutions. Instead, they mainly rely on stitching general-purpose networks, a “tool-driven” paradigm that inevitably results in structural redundancy and bottlenecks in information flow. To fill this gap, this paper proposes Coupler, a wireless native-AI neural backbone designed for the representation learning of channel state information—the pivotal data in wireless systems. Leveraging the physical insights revealed by channel tensors, Coupler decomposes representation learning into individual domains on a layer-by-layer basis and then couples the learned domain-specific features through a dimension-staggered cascade. This full-domain interleaved learning architecture enables superior parameter efficiency and fine-grained multi-domain feature fusion. Based on this backbone, we use complex-domain multilayer perceptrons as spatial and frequency domain learners, while employing three optional mechanisms—convolution, attention, or gating—to capture temporal dependencies. This results in a series of efficient and extremely lightweight channel learning schemes with diverse functionalities, showcasing the compactness, versatility, and flexibility of Coupler. We evaluate these schemes on channel deduction, a general representation task encompassing channel estimation, interpolation, prediction, and feedback. Extensive experimental evaluations validate the significant performance gains and robust applicability, even for real-world measured data, demonstrating Coupler’s potential as a promising basic architecture in the design of wireless foundation models.

title: Human Pose Estimation Using Millimeter-Wave Radar: Prototype, Dataset, and Method
abstract: Three-dimensional human pose estimation (3D-HPE) is important for human-centered sensing, but vision-based solutions are limited by privacy concerns, illumination changes, and occlusion. Although millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar provides a privacy-preserving alternative, existing radar point clouds are often sparse and incomplete, and existing radar 3D-HPE datasets remain limited in subject scale, frame volume, and motion diversity. This paper presents a mmWave radar prototype for dense point-cloud sensing, a large-scale mmWave radar dense human pose estimation (mmWave-DensePose) dataset, and the part-aware spatio-temporal network (PAST-Net) for radar-only 3D-HPE. Specifically, we design a four-chip cascaded mmWave radar system with an azimuth and elevation resolution of 1.30 ° and 2.24 ° , respectively, to generate dense human-related point clouds. The constructed dataset contains 101 subjects, 19 designed motions, numerous free motions, and 570 124 valid synchronized frames. Each valid frame contains 164 valid subject-related radar points on average, exceeding the representative released datasets and providing clearer body-region cues for radar-based 3D-HPE. The proposed method uses only mmWave radar point clouds as input and Kinect V2 skeletons as ground-truth annotations. PAST-Net reorganizes frame-level point-cloud features into skeleton-aware part-token representations and models their temporal evolution through part-wise self-attention, compensating for weak and incomplete observations in local body regions. Experiments on the proposed benchmark show that PAST-Net achieves an average mean localization error of 4.08 cm, reducing the error by 22.14% compared with a state-of-the-art baseline. Ablation results further confirm the contributions of the proposed modules and input features, which include skeleton-aware spatial modeling, part-wise temporal modeling, and radar-specific point attributes. These results demonstrate that the designed mmWave radar prototype and the proposed method provide an effective sensing basis for privacy-preserving and fine-grained 3D-HPE.

title: Sectoral Coordination to Maximize China’s National and Provincial Building Carbon Emissions Mitigation
abstract: The building sector is central to achieving China’s carbon peak and neutrality targets, yet existing assessments seldom integrate full life cycle emissions into subnational policy design. Here we develop a building material–energy–emission (BMEE) model to quantify direct, indirect, and embodied CO 2 emissions from all building types across 31 Chinese mainland provinces from 2000 to 2060 and to evaluate 50 policy scenarios that combine five strategies: urban renewal, green buildings, low-carbon construction, circular economy, and energy transition. The model links dynamic material flow analysis with energy balance sheet splitting, supported by newly compiled national databases on building material and operational energy intensities, and incorporates a renovation module that prioritizes renovation over demolition. We find that China’s building emissions have peaked around 2017 and can decline to between 0.69 and 2.48 Gt (10 9 tonnes) CO 2 by 2060. Under the lowest-emission pathway, cumulative emissions are reduced by 39.5% relative to business-as-usual, with urban renewal providing the largest contribution to total mitigation, followed by green buildings and energy transition. Public buildings, the material sector, and northern provinces exhibit the largest mitigation potentials, while provincial results highlight distinct strategy priorities. Monte Carlo analysis confirms that these conclusions are robust despite widening parametric uncertainty. Our findings underscore the importance of sectoral coordination and regionally tailored policy packages to maximize building decarbonization in China and provide a scalable framework for other large countries facing concurrent new construction and stock-renewal challenges.

title: ECT-VR: Intuitive Teleoperation via Hybrid Virtual–Reality Immersive Interaction with Multi-Sensor Perception for Agricultural Robots
abstract: Fully autonomous robots are still difficult to deploy in complex, unstructured, and dynamic agricultural environments, whereas conventional teleoperation systems suffer from insufficient environmental information and poor spatial intuitiveness. To overcome these limitations, this paper presents enhanced conventional teleoperation with virtual reality (ECT-VR), an immersive teleoperation system for agricultural mobile robots based on hybrid three- and two-dimensional (3D+2D) perception and interaction. The system employs a collaborative architecture that combines a preconstructed global 3D map with real-time local color-depth feedback. In the 3D subsystem, aerial images are processed using structure-from-motion (SfM) and multi-view stereo reconstruction, together with multi-stage post-processing methods, to generate large-scale static agricultural maps for global environmental perception. In the 2D subsystem, an onboard color-depth camera provides real-time visual feedback, while depth data are used for robot pose estimation and local dynamic information during field operations. A Unity3D-based virtual-reality interface synchronizes the virtual robot model with the physical robot and incorporates global positioning visualization, collision-warning visualization, and motion-command feedback. Field experiments conducted at four agricultural and field-relevant outdoor sites, together with a user-centered validation involving 20 participants, show that ECT-VR can support environmental information visualization and robot motion control in agricultural teleoperation. The system achieved an overall mean Likert score of 4.75/5.00 across 11 evaluation items, with an average positive-response proportion of 95.0% for scores ≥ 4. These results suggest that ECT-VR provides user-perceived benefits in information completeness, interaction intuitiveness, operational support, and safety assistance for agricultural robot teleoperation.

title: The Precision Design, Synthesis, and Application of Novel Bioactive Small Molecules to Power the Aquaculture Green Revolution
abstract: Environmentally friendly bioactive small molecules are structurally defined, low-molecular-weight organic compounds that exert biological effects while posing relatively low risk to human health and the environment. Their chemical synthesis and their application as green inputs in aquaculture provide a key pathway to reduce and replace antibiotics and improve quality and efficiency, thereby supporting the sustainable development of the aquaculture industry. This study systematically reviews research advances in the green synthesis and application of five key bioactive small molecules: short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan metabolites, tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle regulators, bile acid derivatives, and the quorum sensing inhibitor bromofuranone C-30. Chemical and physical modifications (e.g., salinization, esterification, and encapsulation) significantly enhance SCFA stability and targeted delivery. Efficient and green synthetic processes, such as Michael addition and Friedel–Crafts alkylation, enable the high-yield, low-cost preparation of indole-3-propionic acid and indole-3-lactic acid (ILA). Furthermore, innovative catalytic oxidation and lactonization routes provide new synthetic strategies for α-ketoglutaric acid and its derivatives. For bile acid derivatives (e.g., ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), sodium taurocholate, and 5α/5β-cyprinol sulfate), novel synthetic and extraction processes featuring streamlined steps, mild conditions, and high atom economy have been developed. A novel two-step synthesis of bromofuranone C-30 enables its scalable production, and a nano-encapsulated sustained-release formulation effectively resolves issues of thermal instability and rapid gastric absorption. These advances overcome the traditional extraction bottlenecks of limited raw materials, cumbersome procedures, and low yields. This review offers theoretical and technical perspectives to advance the targeted design, efficient synthesis, and industrial application of green aquaculture inputs, ultimately contributing to a more sustainable industry marked by greater safety and efficiency.

title: Integrated Suspended Line: A New Heterogeneous Integration for 5G/6G RF Integrated Circuits
abstract: With the evolution of fifth-generation (5G)-advanced and sixth-generation (6G) mobile communication research, the demand for high-performance, miniaturized radio frequency (RF) integrated circuits (ICs) has become increasingly pressing, particularly in emerging 5G/6G air–space–ground–sea integrated communication scenarios that impose stringent requirements on RF front-end performance. As a heterogeneous integration platform, integrated suspended line (ISL) technology alleviates the loss bottleneck of conventional transmission lines by suspending the signal line in an air cavity, thereby reducing both dielectric and radiation losses. Its self-packaging and multilayer integration reduce circuit volume and weight while remaining compatible with 5G/6G air–space–ground–sea integrated RF applications. This paper summarizes the four typical structures of ISL (i.e., substrate integrated suspended line (SISL), metal integrated suspended line (MISL), silicon-based integrated suspended line (Si-ISL), and hybrid integrated suspended line (HISL)), reviews its applications in microwave/millimeter-wave circuits, and discusses its potential in 5G/6G air–space–ground–sea integrated communication systems.

title: Editorial for the Special Issue on the Development of Gut-Microbiome-Targeted Foods and Drugs
Global Terrestrial Photosynthesis Increased Substantially During 2000–2023, Driven by Changing Atmospheric CO2 Concentration, Climate, and Vegetation
abstract: Modeling and prediction of terrestrial gross primary production (GPP) in the globe face many challenges. Here we use the Vegetation Photosynthesis Model (VPM-v4), satellite images, atmospheric CO 2 concentration data, ERA5-Land dataset, and annual land cover maps to estimate global GPP during 2000–2023. At the site scale, annual GPP and its interannual variability (IAV), and the trends from VPM-v4 have strong agreement with those from the eddy covariance tower sites that have ≥ 10 years of measurements, a total of 777 site-years. At the global scale, global annual GPP estimate from VPM-v4 varies from 145 petagrams of carbon per year (Pg C·a −1 ) in 2000 to 166 Pg C·a −1 in 2023, with an increasing trend of 0.78 Pg C·a −2 , which is higher than that from most terrestrial biospheric models (TBMs) and Earth system models (ESMs). The biochemical CO 2 effect on annual GPP varies among the biomes and is high in tropical and subtropical forests and contributes substantially to continued increase of global annual GPP during 2000–2023. In comparison to many TBMs and ESMs, global GPP estimates from VPM-v4 falls within the range of annual GPP estimates from carbonyl sulfide (OCS)-based method (157 Pg C·a −1 ; 2000–2010), respiration-based method (149 Pg C·a −1 ), and 18 O-based method (150–175 Pg C·a −1 ). By integrating a Farquhar–von Caemmerer–Berry model (FvCB)-based representation of the biochemical CO 2 effect into a scalable satellite-based light use efficiency (LUE) framework, this study bridges biochemical photosynthesis theory and global remote-sensing observations, advances the assessment of long-term GPP change, and provides a complementary basis for terrestrial carbon-cycle studies and TBM/ESM evaluation.

title: A High-Efficiency Off-Axis Space Solar Concentrator with Large Tolerance for Acceptance Angle Variations
abstract: The use of solar energy for lunar regolith melting plays a key role in the construction of lunar bases and in-situ resource utilization. In this process, solar concentrators should achieve high efficiency while minimizing the reliance on precise solar tracking, which helps reduce installation costs and precision requirements during space exploration. In this work, we propose an off-axis conjugate point-focus solar concentrator that combines a zero-occlusion triple-mirror configuration with aberration-compensated freeform surfaces to enhance both concentration performance and angular acceptance. The 300 mm-aperture system is optimized to maintain efficient focusing within an acceptance half-angle of ±0.5°, where the acceptance angle is defined as the maximum incidence-angle deviation from the ideal normal incidence for which the concentration ratio remains above 90% of its on-axis value, representing roughly a two-fold improvement in angular tolerance compared with conventional off-axis dish concentrators reported in the literature, while keeping a higher concentration ratio. A feedback-based optical design method is developed, in which a conjugate mirror and iterative adjustment of the mirror normals are used to suppress coma and spherical aberrations and improve the focal-spot energy distribution. Monte Carlo ray-tracing and aberration analysis show that the optimized design achieves a high optical concentration ratio and a compact focal spot with low residual aberrations over the design field of view. Outdoor solar concentration experiments under a solar irradiance of 390 W·m −2 and an ambient temperature of 5 °C demonstrate a peak focal temperature of 892 °C and an effective concentration ratio of 548. Under lunar irradiance with radiative boundary conditions, the model predicts a focal temperature of 1326 °C, which is competitive with previously reported off-axis concentrator systems designed for space applications. These results indicate that the proposed concentrator can provide the high-temperature flux required for lunar regolith melting and other in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) processes, and that its enhanced angular tolerance makes it well suited for deployment on lunar surface platforms and deep-space energy systems.

title: Innovation Trends in Synthetic Biology
High-Performance Grain-Oriented Electrical Steel for a Sustainable and Electrified World
Green Aviation Propulsion: Integrated Innovation Toward Carbon-Neutral Flight
Outburst Floods Redefine Design Floods for Critical Infrastructure in High-Mountain Rivers
abstract: Design floods serve as safety standards for critical infrastructure and flood protection. Conventionally, they are estimated from historical precipitation and streamflow records and therefore largely represent meteorological floods. However, in high-mountain rivers, this practice can severely underestimate actual flood hazards because the most catastrophic events are often geomorphically triggered outburst floods. Here, we present evidence that outburst floods can generate peak discharges that far exceed local 100-year meteorological floods and even surpass the global meteorological flood envelope. We further show that the dominant flood-generating mechanism shifts systematically along the river’s longitudinal profile. Glacial lake outburst floods dominate in U-shaped paraglacial valleys, landslide lake outburst floods in V-shaped fluvial gorges, and meteorological floods in wide alluvial floodplains. Consequently, no single mechanism can adequately define basin-wide safety standards. To address this gap, we propose a unified design flood framework that probabilistically integrates the contributions of these distinct flood-generating processes. This framework redefines design standards to improve the resilience and safety of critical infrastructure in high-mountain regions.

title: Diffusion Strategy of Water Electrolytic Hydrogen in Desert Energy Systems and Ecosystems
abstract: Deploying photovoltaic (PV) systems in desert regions can support both decarbonization and ecological restoration, but conventional photovoltaic-to-grid (PVtG) strategies face increasing integration costs, curtailment, and value deflation as deployment scales up. This study proposes a novel water–energy–ecology coupling mode for desert PV development by integrating PVtG with onsite photovoltaic-to-hydrogen (PVtH) systems through segmented temporal partitioning. To evaluate this nexus, we develop a nonlinear multiscale framework that enables consistent evaluation of how local PV deployment decisions translate into system-wide decarbonization, financial cost, and biomass outcomes. Using the Kubuqi Desert—the seventh largest desert in China—as a testbed, we identify the scaling law of PV utilization by evaluating eight temporal partition strategies across PV capacities up to 25 gigawatts (GW). The results show that pure PVtG strategies exhibit diseconomies of scale, increasing unit cost by 1.6 × 10 −3 USD·(kW·h)⁻ 1 . In contrast, hybrid strategies that allocate peak generation to PVtH reduce system costs by up to 1.0 × 10 −3 USD·(kW·h)⁻ 1 . The cost-efficient 25 GW strategy annually withdraws 25.25 million tonnes (Mt) of water, delivers 25.30 TW·h of electricity, and produces 0.36 Mt of green hydrogen. This strategy achieves a 24 Mt reduction in CO 2 emissions and a 4 × 10 4 t increase in biomass. This hybrid approach outperforms alternatives such as carbon capture and grass pads, with total cost savings of 0.90 billion USD. Sensitivity analysis further reveals that water availability and grid-side storage strongly affect the optimal partition trajectory, while carbon prices of 12.86–15.43 USD·tCO 2 ⁻ 1 can close the financial gap without subsidies. To support implementation, water and land regulations and segmented power purchase agreements (PPAs) are recommended.

title: Second-Scale Fabrication of Chang’e-6 Agglutinate-Inspired Lunar Glass
abstract: Establishing a sustained human presence on the Moon depends on efficiently converting in situ resources into structural materials, thereby reducing the logistical and economic burden of Earth–Moon transport. Agglutinates—complex assemblages of glassy phases, partially melted mineral fragments, and residual crystalline grains formed by micrometeoroid impacts—offer natural templates for high-temperature glass formation. However, the conversion of natural agglutinate structures of lunar soil into engineered glass materials has not been extensively investigated, and conventional furnace-based sintering and hardening techniques for resource utilization typically involve long thermal cycles. In this study, inspired by agglutinates in the Chang’e-6 returned samples, we developed a mineralogically and chemically high-fidelity lunar soil simulant (BH-6) with matched mineral crystal structures, less than 5% deviation in bulk chemical composition, and a median particle size difference of approximately 6 μm. Complete vitrification of compacted BH-6 under vacuum conditions was achieved within approximately 60 s using Joule heating. The resulting glass exhibited a mean relative density of 94.6%, showed no detectable crystalline phases within the detection limit, and exhibited high nanomechanical performance, with hardness exceeding 8.8 GPa and Young’s modulus exceeding 106 GPa. Compared to conventional sintering, this method accelerates the glass formation process by two orders of magnitude, offering a new paradigm for rapid lunar glass production and supporting the future development of rapid, on-demand in situ resource utilization processing.

title: Transfer Learning-Based Framework for Joint Scheduling and Control Across Manufacturing Domains Toward Industry 5.0
abstract: Industry 5.0 is a novel manufacturing paradigm that aims to create human-centric, sustainable, and resilient manufacturing systems by fostering deep collaboration between humans and sophisticated technologies. Stochastic manufacturing environments require adaptable scheduling and control policies for fluctuating conditions such as demand, variable processing times, and frequent equipment failures. Although conventional dispatching rules and control policies are readily implemented, they often yield high scrap rates and excessive maintenance operations. Consequently, reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a data-driven alternative for addressing these issues. Despite its effectiveness, the practical implementation of RL presents several challenges including learning process initialization. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a transfer learning (TL)-based framework for joint scheduling and control in dynamic multi-line manufacturing environments. The objective is to improve production output and energy efficiency through intelligent manufacturing and predictive maintenance, thereby supporting long-term sustainability, human-centric operations, and operational resilience toward Industry 5.0. The proposed framework transfers knowledge from a conventional multi-line manufacturing environment to an additive manufacturing (AM) environment by implementing a long short-term memory network to facilitate the transfer of joint control policies across heterogeneous manufacturing domains. The generalizability and domain adaptation of the framework are evaluated by applying it to an AM environment to jointly control operations, including the printing process and output quality. The results reveal that the domain-adapted network achieves perfect diagonal scores with off-diagonal scores equivalent to zero, indicating that substantially distinct policies are developed for each domain without cross-domain confusion. These findings demonstrate that TL can significantly improve efficiency and reliability in a manufacturing setting, thereby providing a viable approach for practical deployment.

title: Frontiers of Extreme Manufacturing: From Atomic Precision to Autonomous System
Terrain-Aware Autonomy for Self-Reconfigurable Rovers Informed by Zhurong In Situ Datasets from Utopia Planitia
abstract: Terrain-aware autonomy is critical for rovers to safely traverse heterogeneous surfaces. Multimode mobility across loose sand and sharp relief remains challenging because mode switching, which induces mechanical reconfiguration, is constrained by reduced contact stability. This study developed a terrain-aware autonomy control framework incorporating multimode mobility, informed by in situ datasets from China’s Zhurong Mars rover in Utopia Planitia, and subsequently validated it using an Earth-based prototype. In situ traverse logs and imagery spanning 359 sols were analyzed to quantify the wheel–terrain interaction and wheel-rolling mobility limits. Autonomous obstacle-avoidance drives achieved longer traverses per drive than Earth-commanded drives (mean 13.9 m vs 6.1 m), and slip-sinkage statistics were used to update Martian sinkage parameters. Obstacle morphologies extracted from close-range images were further systematically categorized into terrain undulations, surface obstacles, and topographic barriers by linking terrain characteristics to traverse-interruption conditions. A mechanics-constrained action library of 120 maneuvers was constructed and grouped into six basic mobility modes, including body creeping and wheel lifting. A “Look, Touch, and Move” strategy is proposed for multimode decision-making through fuzzy logic safety gating. Efficient waypoint cruising was experimentally demonstrated on a Mars-analog test site using a Zhurong Mars rover prototype, where five representative obstacle types were overcome with online replanning and nine autonomous mode switches.

title: AI-Native 6G: A Paradigm Shift from Enabling Connectivity to Value Realization
abstract: Recent generations of mobile communication systems, particularly the sixth-generation (6G) networks, have become increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence (AI).In this context, AI-native 6G has been investigated from several complementary perspectives, including semantic communications, goal-oriented communications, and agentic communications.While these aspects are essential, they represent only intermediate steps toward the ultimate objective of future intelligent systems enabled by 6G.This commentary argues that the primary role of AI-native 6G should evolve from enabling communications to fulfilling application-specific needs and realizing the goals and value of diverse systems.Due to the dramatically increased complexity of network and application dynamics, achieving this in 6G-enabled systems will rely on embedding intelligence into future network architectures, operational procedures, and collaboration among networked entities.Specifically, we present a value-centric vision in which 6G serves as an AI-native platform that integrates communication, computing, sensing, and physical capabilities to achieve system-level goals.Furthermore, we identify three key autonomous goal-fulfillment and value-realization directions: defining system-level goals through multimodal sensing and cross-domain inference; AI-and trust-native collaborative system operation; and value-centric multidimensional resource orchestration for heterogeneous service provisioning.

title: An Intelligent Framework for Synergistic CO2 Sequestration and Brine Production in Saline Aquifers
abstract: Geological CO 2 storage combined with enhanced water recovery (CO 2 -EWR) can effectively mitigate reservoir pressure buildup while increasing CO 2 storage capacity, thereby providing an effective pressure-management strategy for saline aquifers. However, CO 2 -EWR involves complex hydrogeological processes, and its storage performance is jointly governed by geological properties, well operating parameters, and economic conditions. To address these challenges, this study proposes an intelligent integrated optimization framework for synergistic CO 2 geological storage and brine production. Within this framework, dynamic analysis methods for both brine production and CO 2 injection were first established. By coupling long short-term memory (LSTM) neural-network surrogate models with semi-analytical models, reservoir parameters were inverted and dynamic storage responses were characterized, with relative errors below 5% in the validation cases. Subsequently, a multi-objective particle swarm optimization (MOPSO) algorithm was employed to optimize the injection and production parameters with the dual objectives of maximizing cumulative CO 2 injection volume and net present value (NPV). The surrogate models exhibited strong predictive performance for average reservoir pressure and CO 2 saturation, with coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) ranging from 0.9795 to 0.9998 and maximum normalized root mean square errors (NRMSEs) of 1.67% and 6.52%, respectively. Regarding engineering optimization, brine-derived revenue was particularly important under low-carbon-price conditions, increasing the project NPV by 162% and the cumulative CO 2 injection volume by 184%. Application to field data from the Illinois Basin Decatur Project (IBDP) showed that, after optimization and with brine production incorporated, the CO 2 storage capacity of the target reservoir reached 3.18 × 10 7 m 3 , representing a 2.56-fold increase compared with the case without brine production, while reservoir pressure remained within the prescribed safety limit. Overall, the proposed framework integrates engineering performance and economic profitability and provides a practical decision-support tool for project-specific parameter selection, field-scale CO 2 -EWR scheme comparison, and preliminary project design.

title: Trustworthy Biomedical Microwave Sensing for Long-Term Deployment
Recent Advances in Clinical Neuromodulation for Brain Disorders
abstract: Brain disorders are recognized as dynamic processes driven by molecular and cellular abnormalities, neuronal circuit disturbances, and disrupted brain–body interactions. Compared with traditional drugs, neuromodulation offers circuit-level precision, reversibility, minimal systemic side effects, and durable neuroplasticity-driven benefits, making it the preferred strategy for drug-resistant brain disorders. Advances at the intersection of biomedical engineering, artificial intelligence (AI), electronics, and material science are reshaping clinical neuromodulation techniques. In this review, we summarize recent clinical progress in advanced neuromodulation techniques for brain disorders and outline the pathophysiological foundations of neurological dysfunctions and neuro–organ interactions. We also categorize neuromodulation techniques on the basis of their mechanisms, main targets, and fundamental design principles. Finally, we discuss their clinical applications and how advances in AI and closed-loop systems are reshaping individualized neuronal modulation and intervention techniques. By uniting pathological mechanisms and engineering innovations, neuromodulation is poised to be the future of brain disease treatment and has substantial application potential. Future advances in neuromodulation are less likely to arise from any single device or stimulation modality and instead from integrated therapeutic systems that combine state sensing, multiscale mechanistic understanding, and dynamic intervention control, thereby enabling the development of more individualized and durable strategies for the precise treatment of brain disorders.

title: Artificial Intelligence Empowers Regulatory Compliance Science for Medical Devices: From Premarket Approval to Post-market Surveillance, How Far Are We There?
abstract: While artificial intelligence (AI) in medicine has been extensively studied as a medical device, its role as a governance tool for regulatory authorities remains largely unexplored. The rapid influx of innovative, AI-integrated medical devices has revealed critical bottlenecks in the current human-designed regulatory system (Hud-RS), including approval delays and resource constraints. In this work, we conceptualize a comprehensive dynamic framework for regulatory modernization, termed the “Artificial Intelligence Governance Regulatory System (Aig-RS).” The framework covers the full product lifecycle, from pre-clinical and clinical review to post-market surveillance. We examine current practices across regulatory agencies and propose strategies to optimize existing measures to streamline review processes. Although the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has made significant advances with its agency-wide tool (enterprise language support assistant (ELSA)), timely translation of innovative medical devices into clinical practice remains limited. Accordingly, Aig-RS is intended to accelerate regulatory decision-making safely by leveraging AI and to clarify how regulatory agencies can implement AI across the review continuum.

title: Continuous Low-Temperature Photothermal CO2 Desorption Enables Scalable Solar-Driven Direct Air Capture
abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) is increasingly recognized as an indispensable negative-emission technology for achieving carbon neutrality. However, its practical deployment is severely constrained by energy-intensive CO 2 desorption, high desorption temperature, poor stability, and complex batch operations. Here, we present a continuous low-temperature photothermal CO 2 desorption strategy that enables scalable solar-driven DAC. Photothermal polyethyleneimine–polyethylene glycol (PEI–PEG) functionalized pellets suitable for scalable applications are developed, which simultaneously demonstrate high broadband solar absorptance of 87.4%, good CO 2 adsorption capacity of 1.2 mmol·g −1 , and ultralow desorption temperature of 66 °C. The underlying mechanism is attributed to hydrogen bond cross-linking network of PEI and PEG, stabilizing the anime active sites and reducing the steric hindrance for internal CO 2 diffusion. Building on these materials, a kilogram-scale continuous photothermal CO 2 desorption system is established for the first time via integrating PEI–PEG adsorbent pellets with hourglass inspired self-rolling reactors. Remarkable solar-chemical efficiency of 24.8%, in stark contrast to only 11.5% for discontinuous batch reactor system, is demonstrated due to high pellet solar absorptance, low desorption temperature, and dynamic balance between pellets flow and incident photoenergy. This work establishes a promising pathway toward scalable, efficient, and low-carbon-footprint DAC through continuous low-temperature photothermal CO 2 desorption.

title: From Four-Diagnostic Signals to Trustworthy Clinical Intelligence: Engineering Digital Characterization and AI-Assisted Decision Support in TCM
abstract: Digital methods are increasingly being used to quantify the observations that inform diagnosis and treatment in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), alongside physicians’ clinical judgment. A central challenge is to determine how measurements derived from the Four Diagnostics can support reliable clinical decisions. This review reframes digital characterization in TCM as a system-level engineering problem of moving from signals to evidence and examines the full technical chain from multimodal acquisition to clinical deployment. We summarize recent progress in the engineered acquisition of Four-Diagnostic information and then examine the intermediate steps through which raw Four-Diagnostic data are transformed into computable TCM phenotypes, with emphasis on semantic anchoring, quality validation, multimodal representation learning, knowledge representation, and dynamic phenotyping. Building on this foundation, we review applications of machine learning, knowledge graphs, large language models, and clinical decision support systems in syndrome identification, prescription recommendation, and risk prediction, distinguishing reported model performance from evidence obtained in clinical workflows. Finally, we analyze the major bottlenecks that currently constrain the clinical translation of artificial intelligence (AI) in TCM. Further progress will depend on whether computable phenotypes and model outputs retain their meaning and usefulness across clinical settings, and whether their use improves care under prospective evaluation.

title: GPU-Accelerated Mathematical Programming via First-Order Methods: A New Computational Paradigm for Modern Operations Research
abstract: Modern operations research is entering a new computational era driven by the co-evolution of hardware acceleration and scalable first-order optimization methods. As decision-making problems in power systems, logistics, engineering design, artificial intelligence, and scientific computing grow rapidly in scale, traditional central processing unit (CPU)-centric mathematical programming solvers are increasingly facing fundamental computational bottlenecks. Graphics processing units (GPUs), together with emerging heterogeneous hardware such as quantum processors, matrix accelerators, field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), and other domain-specific accelerators, are therefore not only accelerating existing solvers, but also reshaping the algorithmic paradigms, software architectures, numerical implementations, and application frontiers of mathematical programming. This perspective examines this transition from an algorithm–hardware co-design, with a particular focus on GPU-compatible first-order methods for mathematical programming. We discuss how GPU architectures interact with the main computational patterns of modern solvers. We then examine recent progress in GPU-accelerated linear programming, quadratic programming, conic and nonlinear programming, semidefinite programming, and mixed-integer linear programming, with emphasis on first-order methods, GPU-resident interior-point methods, low-rank formulations, parallel primal heuristics, multi-GPU implementations, and mixed-precision schemes. Finally, we discuss open challenges in robustness and accuracy, scalable solver architectures, and heterogeneous implementation, and argue that algorithm–hardware co-design will become a central foundation for next-generation intelligent decision systems.

title: Aligning Temporal EEG Components: A Framework for Enhanced Motor Decoding
